scope: Published current reconstruction, exact scoped obstruction and normalization theorems, and definitions for bounded replay. No global DELL solution or worldwide priority claim.

equations.title: multiplicative theta convention
equations.assumptions: P is the standard multiplicative coordinate nome; in Koroteev-Shakirov equation3.3 it equals the square of the paper's p. Theta ratios cancel the scalar product factors.

equations.title: momentum shell energy and charge
equations.assumptions: Integer n_i; E is nonnegative and the momentum nome is W. Position nome P and momentum nome W are independent formal parameters.

equations.title: signless normalized DELL current modes
equations.assumptions: The published Koroteev-Shakirov current is reconstructed with the common coordinate Vandermonde divided out and the overall (-1)^a mode sign removed. This defines the tested model; it is not a new DELL construction.

equations.title: common left-factor cancellation
equations.assumptions: Associative operator algebra; M and C0 are invertible in the declared completion. No commutativity of factors is assumed. This identifies raw and theta-ratio current conventions after left normalization.

equations.title: formal normalized Hamiltonian recurrence
equations.assumptions: H_a=C0^(-1)*Ca; products are ordinary for classical functions and ordered for quantum difference operators. Every coefficient uses finitely many earlier coefficients.

equations.title: current charge recurrence
equations.assumptions: For the literal signless current, shift every n_i by1. Ratios depend only on differences. In the quantum action convention the total shift commutes with all coordinate-ratio coefficients. Formal Laurent W interpretation handles negative a.

equations.title: finite shell completeness
equations.assumptions: All scalar summands are nonnegative on integers. Enumerating precisely this finite coordinate range and filtering total E and charge is exhaustive at every declared momentum order.

equations.title: logarithmic canonical Poisson bracket
equations.assumptions: Classical independent nonzero multiplicative coordinates. Exact jet derivatives are computed before rational specialization; evaluating a zero bracket at finitely many points alone is not a global identity proof.

equations.title: integrable deformation compatibility
equations.assumptions: Coefficient equation for formal Poisson commutativity. The new order enters linearly; no general solvability or completeness is asserted.

equations.title: canonical deformation equivalence
equations.assumptions: An infinitesimal canonical change of coordinates. This is a gauge equivalence of first-order corrections, not a classification of all DELL systems.

equations.title: three-particle first-shell expansion
equations.assumptions: Coordinate nome P=0; A has six permutation shifts(-1,0,1), B has three shifts(-1,1,1), C has three shifts(2,0,0). Equations use signless oriented coefficients.

equations.title: exact first-shell Poisson cancellation
equations.assumptions: Classical N=3,P=0. Sparse Laurent-polynomial numerator cancellation proves rational identities in symbolic T,X,Y; this is stronger than sampled evaluations, and is only first order in W.

equations.title: common-power normalization rigidity
equations.assumptions: Classical P=0,N=3; common exponent s. The nonzero exact witness forces s=1 for an identity over generic parameters. Not a full normalizer classification outside this ansatz.

equations.title: six-mode first-order normalizer classification
equations.equation: rho=sum_(n in perm(-1,0,1))lambda_n(T)*F_n*Y^n; {C1/(1+W rho),C2/(1+W rho)}=O(W²) iff all lambda_n=1
equations.assumptions: Classical N=3,P=0. The lambda_n depend on coupling T only. Valid at T!=0,1; the exact rank certificate excludes further exceptional nonzero couplings within these six fixed functions.

equations.title: normalizer rank and coupling boundary
equations.assumptions: M6 is the retained six-row coefficient minor of the normalizer compatibility map. At T=1 the six coefficients are unconstrained at first order. Zero coupling is excluded by the Laurent current definition.

equations.title: standard trigonometric Ruijsenaars weights
equations.equation: a_I(X;T)=prod_(i in I,j notin I)(T Xi-Xj)/(Xi-Xj); H1f=sum_i a_i f(Yi); H2f=sum_(i<j)a_ij f(Yi)f(Yj)
equations.assumptions: N=3 and unchanged standard coordinate coefficients; one common meromorphic particlewise momentum profile f. This ansatz is narrower than a general DELL family.

equations.title: particlewise momentum obstruction identity
equations.assumptions: K1(T)=(5T^4-26T^3+126T-105)/72. A second coordinate witness X=(1,2,5) has K2(T)=(7T^4-27T^3+90T-70)/16; a retained Bezout identity proves the only common coupling root is T=1.

equations.title: classified particlewise profile
equations.assumptions: Two independent coordinate witnesses and an exact Bezout identity close all exceptional couplings except T=1. Nonconstant meromorphic f on a connected logarithmic cover gives local powers; globally single-valued on C* forces integer lambda. At T=1 arbitrary momentum profiles commute.

equations.title: particlewise ellipticization no-go
equations.equation: f(PY)=f(Y),0<abs(P)<1 and f(Y)=C*Y^m,m in Z => m=0
equations.assumptions: Together with the classified unchanged-coordinate ansatz this excludes nonconstant single-valued elliptic particlewise profiles at T!=1. It does not exclude general double-elliptic systems or coupled momentum interactions.

equations.title: explicit failed momentum ellipticization direction
equations.assumptions: An exact nonzero first-order direction within the particlewise ansatz. This is a Laurent test profile, not itself an elliptic function; monomial profiles provide positive controls.

equations.title: forced mixed momentum Fourier mode
equations.assumptions: N=3 signless normalized current; the numerator first shell has no(-1,2,0) mode, while C0^(-1)C1 supplies this product. Nonzero generic meromorphic coefficient; no assertion of a new unknown Hamiltonian.

equations.title: ordered quantum coefficient multiplication
equations.assumptions: Literal action S_i f(X)=f(X1,...,Q Xi,...,XN). Q is the quantum shift parameter, distinct from both elliptic nomes; finite coefficient checks do not prove the full quantum commutativity conjecture.

equations.title: right normalization is simultaneous conjugacy
equations.assumptions: Invertible C0 in an associative completed operator algebra. Left and right families have equivalent commutativity; right normalization is not a valid noncommutativity negative control.

equations.title: coefficientwise quantum commutator gate
equations.assumptions: Every ordered output-shift coefficient is tested exactly at the declared rational parameter specializations and finite truncation. The retained receipt, rather than this formula, records which bounded panels actually passed.

equations.title: global second momentum-order Poisson cancellation
equations.assumptions: N=3, rational identity in symbolic T,X,Y. The three exact numerators over Delta^5 have19902,13548,19902terms and cancel coefficientwise. This is finite-order commutativity, not all-order integrability.

equations.title: second-order homogeneous normalizer rank
equations.assumptions: P=0,N=3. A21function ansatz of symmetric products of first-shell functions has generic full rank. Hence no nonzero W² denominator correction in that ansatz at couplings where this minor is nonzero. A vanishing minor alone does not prove a rank drop.

equations.title: global first mixed-nome compatibility
equations.assumptions: N=3. Exact Laurent-polynomial identities in all T,X,Y, with P the product nome. The mixed raw3696terms and normalizer6864terms cancel after denominator clearing; no extrapolation to all elliptic orders.

equations.title: coordinate-deformed first-shell rigidity
equations.equation: lambda_n(T,P)=1 mod P² for all six first-shell functions
equations.assumptions: The global mixed-nome identity supplies a solution; the invertible constant-coordinate-nome minor makes both coefficients unique for each fixed T!=0,1. Numerator modes and six-function normalizer ansatz are fixed.

equations.title: multiaffine profile obstruction
equations.assumptions: g(y)=y*fprime(y),z=f(u),s=f(v),s!=0. Base Hamiltonians are multiaffine and commute in log-canonical variables. A nonzero restricted P1 polynomial forces a nonconstant common profile to be a local power.

equations.title: local coordinate-elliptic no-go extension
equations.equation: T!=0,1 and abs(P)<delta(T) => no nonconstant elliptic particlewise profile in the unchanged elliptic-RS ansatz
equations.assumptions: Conditional on the standard commuting multiaffine elliptic-RS weights holomorphic near P=0 with the declared trigonometric limit. A nonzero P=0 witness persists analytically. No numerical delta or all-moduli classification is claimed.

equations.title: DELL homogeneity and moment-map descent
equations.equation: sum_i Xi*d_Xi H_a=0; sum_i Yi*d_Yi H_a=a*H_a; {H_a,Y_all}=0
equations.assumptions: Directly from current coefficients depending on coordinate ratios and fixed momentum charge. The formal Hamiltonians descend under regular simultaneous-position-scaling reduction at fixed nonzero Y_all.

equations.title: generic formal functional independence
equations.assumptions: At P=W=0,T=1 the normalized currents give elementary symmetric polynomials. This nonzero specialization proves generic independence of H1,...,H_(N-1),Y_all and their regular reduced family in the formal deformation; it does not prove commutativity or convergence.

equations.title: complete second-order normalizer boundary
equations.equation: dim ker(T on actual productfunctions)=1 at T=-1;19 at T=1;0 at all other nonzero T
equations.assumptions: The first denominator shell is fixed to A and the second correction lies in products of its six functions. Three symbolic21minors and exact exceptional-field rank certificates classify all nonzero couplings. Function-space dependencies are quotiented out.

equations.title: resonant freedom is an existing integral
equations.assumptions: A retained nine-product expansion proves membership in the second-order normalizer ansatz. This is one nonzero homogeneous normalizer direction, not a new independent conserved quantity.

equations.title: cube-root coefficient redundancy
equations.assumptions: Zero-based f_i order is lexicographic perm(-1,0,1). The21nominal products span19actual functions. The two coefficient-kernel directions represent identically zero functions, so they give no new normalizer freedom.
